A device used to raise and lower sound volume.
An Italian princess.

Inside, Italian principessas rubbed shoulders with Seventh Avenue princes.
Italian principessas were always there with publishers, playboys, and princes some of the habitués of the club mingling with starlets and socialites.

senses: A machine for cleaning metal, having rotating brushes covered with bran or similar-textured material.
A worker who operates this machine.
To use or spread propaganda.
To tell propaganda to someone in an attempt to influence one's views.
To use something or someone in propaganda purposes.
examples: He propagandized this panacea with single-minded determination throughout the revolutionary period and even managed to establish a People's Bank for a short time before his arrest in 1849.

senses: A Central Asian bun stuffed with meat and sometimes with vegetables.
ety: From Central Asian Turkic, from Classical Persian سَنْبوسَه (sanbōsa), from Middle Persian *sambōsag. Doublet of samosa and sambuseh.

senses: Physically or chemically unaffected by high temperatures
A person who escapes.
American and Oxford British standard spelling of standardise.
The role or office of a steward; stewardship.
The jurisdiction of a steward, or the lands under such jurisdiction.
ety: From Middle English stevardry, stevartry, stewartry, equivalent to steward + -ry.

senses: A sweet or savoury Indian rice dish.
ety: Borrowed from Tamil பொங்கல் (poṅkal, literally “boiling, bubbling up”). Doublet of Pongal.

senses: Any agent that produces relaxation.
A cream or lotion that loosens curls in the hair to aid straightening.
A person who relaxes.
examples: Are you a doer or a relaxer? If you said “some of both,” then you're right on track.

senses: Any object or system that resonates
A hollow cavity whose dimensions are selected so as to resonate at a specific frequency
A resonant electronic circuit
A type of musical instrument, especially a guitar, that uses spun metal resonator cones to enhance the sound.
The property of some crystals of transmitting different colors of light in different directions.
Long and thin, like a stalk of a plant.
Of a plant, having stalks.
Resembling or characteristic of a stalker; seeming to hunt or covertly follow a person.
examples: I peeped between the stalky parts of the Lindsays’ lilacs.

senses: The art or trade of candlemaking.
A business, shop or warehouse used in candlemaking.
An operation (usually, a business) which provides supplies.
The merchandise of a chandler.
ety: From Middle French chandelerie, from chandelier (“chandler”). Equivalent to candle + -ery.

senses: The characteristic cry of a sheep or a goat.
ety: From Middle English bleten, from Old English blǣtan (“to bleat”), from Proto-West Germanic *blātijan, from Proto-Germanic *blētijaną (“to bleat”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₁- (“to howl, cry, bleat”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to make a loud noise”). Cognate with Scots blete, bleit, West Frisian bâlte, blaaien, blêtsje (“to bleat”), Dutch blaten (“to bleat”), Low German bleten (“to bleat”), German blaßen, blässen (“to bleat”).

senses: Acting as if on drugs; torpid, uncoordinated, etc.
A small settlement in the Americas, especially of Native Americans.
A political division denoting a small poor rural settlement.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish ranchería. Doublet of rancherie.
examples: As for escaping, there were eight hundred miles of dry wilderness between the ranchería and civilization.

senses: A clear seasoned broth made by simmering usually light meat, such as beef or chicken.
A similar broth made by reconstituting, that is, by adding hot water to dried powder concentrate; the dried powder concentrate itself.
An excrescence on a horse's frush or frog.
ety: First attested 1656, from French bouillon, from the verb bouillir (“to boil”), from Old French boillir, from Latin bullīre (“to bubble, boil”), from bulla (“bubble”).

senses: The world or sphere of romantic couples.
The state of being a romantic couple.
examples: The ads were already showing as he clambered along and in their patchy glare he loomed and ducked and apologized, and was a clumsy intruder in a world of snuggling coupledom.
More coffee is consumed, a movie date is arranged, coupledom achieved and, naturally, nuptials performed.

senses: A herbivorous mythological creature of the Central African Congo, similar to the unicorn. Its horns are said to be an antidote to poisons, and it has brown fur, two crooked horns and a boar's tail.
ety: From Portuguese abada (“female rhinoceros”), from Malay badak (“rhinoceros”).

senses: A film using smell-o-vision technology.
That does not use or generate gas.
ety: From gas (“state of matter, chemical element, mixture”) + -less.

senses: A card game resembling chemin de fer with many forms, usually entailing the player(s) betting against two or three hands dealt, and also bearing some similarities to blackjack.
ety: First attested in the 19th century. Borrowed from French baccarat, baccara, likely named after the French town Baccarat (noted for glassmaking) in Grand Est, of ultimately unclear and debated origin (first attested in 1291. (uncertain)). If by some Vulgar Latin *Bacchara, the town is possibly named from Latin Bacchi ara ("altar of Bacchus"; the original pagan reference of the name was forgotten), name of an ancient Roman castellum, of which there remains a relic called the "Tower of Bacha" on the heights of Deneuvre, from whence Baccarat is an ancient suburb. senses: A form of Japanese rice wine, less alcoholic than saké and used in cooking.
examples: Although naturally brewed mirin is made from only water, sweet brown rice, and rice koji, much of the mirin sold in natural food stores and Oriental markets is sweetened with sugar or corn syrup; read labels carefully.

senses: Someone who espouses sedevacantism.
One who receives a gift.
A popular Japanese dish consisting of a breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet served in bite-sized pieces and often accompanied by shredded cabbage and miso soup.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 豚カツ (tonkatsu, “pork cutlet”), from 豚 (ton, “pork”) + カツ (katsu, “cutlet”), shortened from カツレツ (katsuretsu).

senses: Evil speech.
ety: From late Middle English malediccion, from Middle French malédiction, from Latin maledictiō (“curse”) from malus (“evil”) + dictiō (“speech”) noun of action from perfect passive participle dictus (“spoken”), from verb dīcō (“speak”).

senses: The state or quality of being supervenient, of being in a dependency relationship such that an object with the supervened properties must also have the supervening properties.
A boy who delivers newspapers to houses on a paper round.
examples: Our current paperboy does a nicely consistent job of throwing the paper onto the porch. Our old paperboy sometimes would fling it into the bushes!

senses: A practitioner or adherent of textualism.
examples: In a 2015 appearance at Harvard Law School, Justice Kagan said that textualism had triumphed across the ideological spectrum. “We’re all textualists now,” she said then.

senses: Erotic literature.
ety: Blend of literature + erotica. Genericized from the trademark Literotica held by Sunlane Media for the free erotic fiction website literotica.com, which started in 1998.
examples: Many people like erotica, and fanfiction plays into the field of literotica, engaging with the reader’s desires intellectually.

senses: Any large rod-shaped virus of the family Baculoviridae, including the granuloviruses and nucleopolyhedroviruses.
ety: From baculo- + virus, from Latin baculum (“rod”).

She shared a particularly adorable video captioned, “all the kisses. happy fall.”, that shows Myron wriggling around on the couch during an after-walkie snuggling session.

senses: bioprosthesis
ety: From bio- + prosthetic. By surface analysis, bio- + prosth- + -etic.

senses: Disinclined to work; lazy.

senses: A variety of chili (a dried chilaca), used especially in sauces.
ety: From the Spanish pasilla, diminutive of pasa (“raisin”).
